newsitem.title: GERMANY: Duisenberg says unsure of chances to be ECB chief.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg says unsure of chances to be ECB chief.

text.p: The incoming president of the European Monetary Institute said on Monday that he was uncertain of his chances of being appointed first head of the future European Central Bank.
Wim Duisenberg, who has declared his interest in the position, said he still hoped to take up the post when the new central bank is formed from the EMI in 1998.
The new central bank will take up monetary policy for the new euro after the single currency's launch in January 1999.
Asked by journalists at a ceremony to mark the departure of EMI President Alexandre Lamfalussy how he saw his chances, Duisenberg said, "I don't know."

Duisenberg, who is Dutch central bank governor, said that it was "very good" to learn that Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer had endorsed him to be the first European Central Bank president in a radio interview on Sunday.
Juergen Stark, state secretary in the German finance ministry, declined to offer a clear endorsement for Duisenberg.
"Duisenberg now has about 12 months time or until about the end of April to fulfil the very high expectations that we have placed on him," Stark told journalists.
Duisenberg will officially become the new president of the EMI on Tuesday at a council meeting.
